issues.title: The cutover runner catches only StepFailed and CalledProcessError, so any other exception skips the report the docstring promises.
issues.why: run_steps catches only (StepFailed, CalledProcessError), and main() writes the report only after run_steps returns. step_production reads the production health log with no exists/empty guard, shell() has no timeout, and OSError from rclone/arm.touch or IndexError on an empty log escape, so a mid-cutover failure on a host being changed leaves no report, against the module docstring. Most individual triggers are unlikely, but the broken guarantee is in new code; the author accepted it as review F002 and widened the handler and added log_tail in 94beba1b.

issues.title: The assertion that cron commands carry no user field can never fail.
issues.why: block_commands returns the command text, which starts with the absolute checkout path, so c.split('/')[0] is always '' and the assertion is vacuous. It is a test-quality defect only; the production code it covers is correct. haiku 1/1's added point, that the report test never calls main(), is also a test gap.

issues.title: The new with_replication branch of provision_tick_roles.sql runs in no database-backed test.
issues.why: The REPLICATION branch is checked only by text order in the unit test; the DB fixture applies the file without with_replication. The branch is copied from provision_roles.sql and reads correctly (\if :{?with_replication}, format(... %I REPLICATION) with \gexec), so this is a missing test for a path with no shown defect.

issues.title: Step 2 runs setup-backup --check before provisioning, and setup-backup dies when 17/tick is not in pg_lsclusters.
issues.why: setup-backup.sh dies in check mode too when a table cluster is absent from pg_lsclusters, and step_check runs before step_provision, which is the step that can pg_createcluster. On manta9000, the only host this cutover targets, 17/tick already exists, as the finding itself says, so the run is not blocked. It matters only for a hypothetical fresh-host use of a one-off script.

issues.title: tick_locks_held builds SQL with an f-string and env_value interpolates the library path into bash -c.
issues.why: Both interpolations exist, but the SQL values are two integer constants and the library path is the script's own checkout location. No input that could break or inject arrives here; it is rule-conformance hardening.

issues.title: Host constants (the '-' sentinel, ARM_FILE, RCLONE_REMOTE, bucket key, cluster names, paths) are defined in several places.
issues.why: The duplicates exist across Python and shell (ARM_FILE in setup-backup.sh:80 and cutover:69, RCLONE_REMOTE, TABLE_NONE, 17/tick in regexes, the date format in step_weekly). None currently disagrees, so this is a maintainability and DRY point with no wrong behavior at head.

issues.title: strip_new_args hard-codes --replication-host 127.0.0.1 instead of reading it from the table row.
issues.why: The literal is present and duplicates the 17/main row value. If the row changed, the TD3 comparison would report a change and stop the cutover, which fails safe. It agrees with the table today; the author changed it later (F003) as cleanup.

issues.title: The report is named by date only, so a same-day re-run overwrites the failed run's report.
issues.why: The report path is NOTES_DIR/<date>-227-cutover.md and is written with write_text, so a same-day re-run replaces it. The failure output also went to the terminal, and the cost is lost audit notes, not wrong behavior.

issues.title: The cutover writes provision and setup output into the notes directory without the log_scrub pass the provision script uses.
issues.why: True that no scrub runs before report.write_text. provision_tick_cluster.sh passes passwords through stdin and PGPASSWORD and prints no secrets, so this is defence-in-depth against output that is not shown to occur.

issues.title: b2_lifecycle.sh captures rclone's stderr with 2>&1 into the JSON it parses with jq.
issues.why: RULES=$(... rclone backend lifecycle ... 2>&1) merges stderr into the rule list, so any rclone notice makes jq's type check fail and setup-backup reports MISSING lifecycle-read, failing the check. This is the known bug, fixed in 0ccf9b00 after it broke cutover step 2 under sudo.

issues.title: test_setup_backup.py has grown to 1072 lines.
issues.why: The file grew from 812 to 1072 lines in this diff. File size is a style point.

issues.title: production_changes strips the new arguments only from the new file, so every re-run after cron installation fails step 4.
issues.why: step_check stores the installed cron file as old_cron; after a first run that file already has --url-key etc. production_changes strips only the new side, so identical files compare unequal and step_apply raises StepFailed. That breaks the documented recovery ('fix the cause, re-run') for any failure after step 4. The author fixed it as F001 in 94beba1b by stripping both sides.

issues.title: run_health ignores the health command's result and can judge a stale last log line.
issues.why: run_health discards shell()'s result and reads the last line of an append-only log. backup_health_cron.sh writes a FAIL cannot_check line on most failures, which health_flags rejects; a stale pass needs the script to exit before logging (argument errors) right after an earlier clean run with the same command. The gap is true but needs unlikely conditions.

issues.title: On a cluster that never archived, pg_settings.sh never persists archive_command because it shows as (disabled).
issues.why: pg_settings.sh reports a (disabled) archive_command as PENDING RESTART and never adds it to DRIFTED, so the tick enrolment would restart into archive_mode=on with no command; the 2026-10-05 cutover run hit this and d14f8a60 fixed it. The claim is correct and the new tick enrolment exposes it, but the defective code in deploy/lib/pg_settings.sh was not changed in base..head, and the case file excludes d14f8a60 for that reason.

issues.title: After an offsite upload failure, re-running step_weekly cannot resume because backup_prod.sh refuses an existing destination.
issues.why: step_weekly skips only when today's base dir and the arm file both exist; otherwise it reruns the full weekly job, and backup_prod.sh exits on 'destination already exists'. The re-run fails loudly and the operator can delete the local dir or wait a day, so it is a recovery inconvenience, not wrong data.

issues.title: step_apply rejects pg_settings' pre-restart DRIFT lines, so the first enrolment of tick always stops at step 4.
issues.why: run_lib echoes all of pg_settings.sh's output, including the DRIFT lines printed before ALTER SYSTEM. archive_mode stays DRIFT 'on' 'off' until the restart in step 5. APPLY_ALLOWED admits only PENDING RESTART and arm-file lines, so setup_not_ok flags them and step 4 fails before the restart. The 2026-10-05 run stopped at step 4 this way, and d14f8a60 added r'^DRIFT 17/tick archive_mode ' to APPLY_ALLOWED.

issues.title: assert is used for type narrowing in runtime code (block_commands, run_health).
issues.why: Both asserts are present, but each is unreachable as a failure: _job_lines already filtered on the same regex, and require() raises before the assert in run_health. Stripping them under -O changes nothing; it is style.

issues.title: production_lines identifies the host block by the cron user field 'root'.
issues.why: The check j.split()[5] == 'root' exists and depends on the host jobs running as root, which the template fixes. It is a field of a root-owned generated file, not a user-visible label, and it is correct today; a robustness point.

issues.title: The provisioning tests assert on shell and SQL source text instead of behaviour.
issues.why: The new tests regex-extract script text and compare substrings and positions. That is a test-design point; no production defect follows from it.

issues.title: Provisioning drops trading_tick_proof and the MT_PROOF_226_* keys while the 226 proof harness still references them.
issues.why: The removal is deliberate: the slice design at head says the proof database is gone and the MT_PROOF_226_* lines are stale. The harness and TICK_PROOF_DB_NAME are left as dead references to a one-off proof, a cleanup point rather than a regression.

issues.title: The cutover tests leave step_apply, step_check, step_offsite and main() untested, and the render test exempts a nonexistent @192.
issues.why: Those steps have no tests, and test_setup_backup.py:777 replaces '@192' although no '@192' exists under deploy/, which weakens the placeholder check (removed later in 229fa4de). These are test gaps and test quality, not production defects.
